subject: Civil Engineering
title: Sulfate Attack
description: Learn Sulfate Attack in one minute.

hook.text: Foundations in sulfate-rich soil expand and crumble — the concrete destroys itself from within.

buildup.text: Sulfates react with aluminate compounds in cement, forming ettringite — a crystal that expands.

discovery.text: Type V cement has low aluminate content — it resists sulfate attack in harsh soils.

twist.text: Low w/c ratio also helps — denser concrete slows sulfate penetration dramatically.

climax.text: The Middle East uses sulfate-resistant concrete extensively — gypsum-rich desert soils demand it.

punchline.text: Know your soil chemistry. The wrong cement in the wrong ground self-destructs.

quiz.question: How does sulfate attack damage concrete?
options: Sulfates dissolve the aggregate, leaving hollow voids
Sulfates react with cement compounds to form expanding crystals that crack the concrete
Sulfate gases corrode the rebar inside the concrete
